public_prompt: Every new customer tier needs a code change in the rate limiter and a redeploy; the limiter is now an 800-line branch tree. What the group intends: the branches are ugly, so replace them with a lookup table in the same module. Identify the defect and state the correction.
observable_resources: limiter/limiter.py — 800 lines; token-bucket arithmetic interleaved with per-tier branches
limiter/change-log.csv — 34 of the last 40 changes altered only per-tier numbers, and all 34 required a redeploy
limiter/table-method.diff — replaces the branches with a literal table in the same file; adding a tier still requires a redeploy
limiter/ops-request.md — support needs to add a tier without a release, and to try a tier's numbers against yesterday's traffic before it goes live
closure:release-cadence-commitment — closed; promises weekly releases as the way to ship tier changes
closure:support-tiering-sla — closed; derived from closure:release-cadence-commitment, promises tier changes within a week
closure:limiter-fleet-sizing — closed; sizes the limiter fleet from peak traffic; rests on the traffic forecast, not on where the tier numbers live

protected_gold.root_success_rubric: PASS iff the specified design moves the per-tier numbers out of the deployed artefact into data that is loaded and validated at runtime, leaves a single enforcement engine that never changes per tier, and supports trying a tier's numbers before activation — and the answer states that an in-module table still requires a redeploy. FAIL if the fix is the table refactor, one feature flag per tier, or a faster release train.

source_provenance: no external dataset; every figure is authored for this benchmark and is not an empirical finding
notes: A solver that keeps the tidy-the-branches framing ships the table; the change log shows 34 of 40 changes were data, and the table leaves every one of them a redeploy.
